climate.overview_html: The dominant status change on September 5 is the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster: at least 1,287 people are now confirmed dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 still missing in Nepal and 531 in Tibet — a combined toll of at least 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing, substantially higher than the 1,100 dead and 4,500 missing reported on September 4. The Super El Niño backdrop established by WMO’s unprecedented September 3 statement — assigning nearly 100% probability that El Niño will persist through February 2027 and describing the event as potentially “literally off the charts” — remains the defining climate signal of the week. European wildfires and drought continue at 647,375 ha burnt area with very extreme fire danger forecast through September 9; and Hurricane Lowell’s re-intensification to Category 5 over Super El Niño–warmed waters, now threatening Hawaii, provides the direct physical link between the ENSO event and the most acute tropical hazard in the Pacific basin.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: STATUS CHANGE — Death Toll Rises to 1,287+ in Nepal + 31 in Tibet = 1,318+; Missing Now 5,083 in Nepal + 531 in Tibet = 5,614+; Flood Debris Reached India 240 km Downstream
items.summary: The confirmed death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse has risen substantially: at least 1,287 people dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet as of September 5 reporting — for a combined total of at least 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing, up from the 1,100 dead and 4,500 missing reported September 4. The disaster originated when a substantial section of Langtang Lirung glacier broke away at approximately 5,200 metres, generating a seismic signal of magnitude Ms 5.2 detected worldwide. Debris temporarily dammed the Lhende River before breaking, releasing a catastrophic flood that struck a 72 km corridor along the Trishuli River in Nepal and the Gyirong checkpoint on the China-Nepal border. Flood-borne debris has now been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police continue search operations; Chinese authorities continue to warn that surrounding glaciers 'may still collapse.' The disaster is one of the deadliest glacial outburst floods on record globally.

items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Nearly 100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February 2027; 2027 Could Be Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — literally off the charts we have used for the past four decades.' WMO assigned nearly 100% probability — its highest ever expressed certainty in an El Niño/La Niña advisory — that El Niño will persist through at least February 2027. Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 record on the multi-variate ENSO index. Because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, peak atmospheric warming will arrive in 2027, raising the prospect of 2027 becoming the warmest year on record.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: 647,375 Hectares Burned — Very Extreme Fire Danger Extended Through September 9 Across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey, Ukraine; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area of 647,375 hectares, with very extreme fire danger forecast through September 9 across a broad arc from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The atmospheric blocking pattern responsible for Europe's exceptional heat and drought has strengthened rather than weakened. The 2026 season is tracking ahead of the same date in the 2025 record season (1,034,552 ha final tally). The Rhine remains at its lowest level since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

items.headline: Climate Change Is Now Europe’s Biggest Systemic Security Threat — 10,000 Excess Deaths From June Heatwave; 9M Tonnes Crop Loss; Military Assets Diverted to Fire Suppression and Flood Defense
items.summary: Chatham House published a policy analysis concluding that climate change is now Europe's biggest systemic security risk. The summer of 2026 provides the evidence base: extreme heat contributed to an estimated 10,000 excess deaths during the June heatwave alone and destroyed approximately 9 million tonnes of crops. The security dimension is direct: Europe's armed forces are increasingly deployed to fight fires, reinforce flood defenses, evacuate populations, and restore critical infrastructure — diverting capacity from conventional security operations. Rhine water levels fell to their lowest since 1880. Chatham House argues climate adaptation investment has structurally lagged behind mitigation spending and that European security planning must treat climate hazard as a primary threat category.

items.headline: NOAA August ENSO Diagnostic: Niño 3.4 Reaches +2.7°C Week of August 12; All 15 Ensemble Members Forecast Peak >+2.5°C; >90% Probability “Very Strong” Event Sept–Nov 2026; No La Niña Transition Before Spring 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's August 2026 ENSO Diagnostic confirms El Niño is tracking toward historically extreme territory. The Niño 3.4 index reached +2.7°C in the week centered on August 12 — already exceeding the +2.5°C 'very strong' threshold. All 15 coupled model ensemble members forecast Niño 3.4 exceeding +2.5°C at the September–November peak; a majority project exceedance of +3.0°C, which would qualify this event as a 'Super El Niño' comparable to 2015–16. NOAA assigns greater than 90% probability to a very strong event during September–November 2026 with little indication of a transition away from El Niño before spring 2027. The September 3 WMO update reinforced this with even higher certainty language.

major_events.name: Hurricane Lowell (Central Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Re-Intensified to Category 5 (160 mph); Hawaii Governor Green Declares Statewide Emergency; CPHC: Hurricane Watches for Kauai County Expected Saturday; Sharp North Turn Sunday; Close Approach Kauai Late Monday; Only 8th Cat 5 in Central Pacific on Record
major_events.status: CATEGORY 5 RE-INTENSIFIED · 160 MPH · STATEWIDE EMERGENCY DECLARED · KAUAI WATCHES EXPECTED SATURDAY · SHARP NORTH TURN SUNDAY · KAUAI LATE MONDAY
major_events.impact: Hurricane Lowell re-intensified from Category 4 (140 mph) to Category 5 with maximum sustained winds near 160 mph as of the September 4 5 p.m. advisory — becoming only the eighth Category 5 hurricane on record in the central Pacific and the first since Hurricane Walaka in 2018. It went from 70-mph tropical storm to 160-mph Category 5 in just over 30 hours, one of the fastest intensifications ever recorded in the central Pacific. Governor Josh Green declared a statewide emergency covering all of Hawaii to allow pre-positioning of resources. CPHC warned that hurricane watches could be required for portions of Kauai County on Saturday. The storm is forecast to drift westward through Saturday before a weakening ridge triggers a sharp northward turn on Sunday, bringing the center close to the western Hawaiian Islands late Monday and Monday night at or near major hurricane strength. Outer rainbands are expected to bring 3 to 6 inches of rain to Kauai and the Big Island, with localized totals exceeding 10 inches; life-threatening surf and rip currents are already impacting all island shores. High surf advisory in effect through Saturday morning for south- and east-facing shorelines.

major_events.name: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods — STATUS CHANGE: 1,287+ Dead in Nepal + 31 in Tibet = 1,318+ Total; 5,083+ Missing in Nepal + 531 in Tibet = 5,614+ Total; Debris Reached India 240 km Downstream; Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing
major_events.status: 1,318+ DEAD · 5,614+ MISSING · DEBRIS REACHED INDIA · BARRIER LAKE RISK · RESCUE ONGOING
major_events.impact: The combined death toll from the August 27 Nepal-Tibet glacier collapse has risen to at least 1,287 confirmed dead in Nepal plus 31 in Tibet, with at least 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet — up from 1,100 dead and 4,500 missing reported September 4. Flood debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. Chinese authorities continue to warn that glaciers surrounding the impact crater 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.' An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police are conducting search operations; helicopter supply runs continue to cut-off communities. Officials warn the death toll will rise further as teams reach previously inaccessible areas.

major_events.name: Malaysia / SE Asia Wildfire Haze — STATUS CHANGE: Malaysia Declares Emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak (API 521); 647 Schools Closing Monday; Cloud-Seeding Launched; Singapore 3rd Worst Air Quality Globally September 4; Indonesia 717 Hot Spots
major_events.status: SERIAN EMERGENCY DECLARED · API 521 · 647 SCHOOLS CLOSING · CLOUD-SEEDING · SINGAPORE 3RD WORST GLOBALLY
major_events.impact: Malaysia declared an emergency in the Serian Division of Sarawak state after the Air Pollutant Index breached the emergency threshold of 500, peaking at 521 on September 4. King Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration; Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's office announced 647 schools will close from Monday until at least end of next week. Malaysia launched a three-day cloud-seeding operation to attempt to ease the hazardous haze. Serian remains at hazardous-level API readings (376) as of September 5 morning. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry satellite data shows 717 fire hot spots nationally since August 1, with 103 active in the past 24 hours. Singapore recorded the third-worst air quality globally on September 4 by IQAir index. The Philippines, Brunei, and northern Malaysia remain under haze impact as El Niño conditions sustain drought and fire risk across Kalimantan through early October.

major_events.name: Hurricane Marie (Eastern Pacific) — STATUS CHANGE: Upgraded to Category 2 (100 mph); Strengthened From Category 1 (80 mph); No Landfall Forecast
major_events.status: CATEGORY 2 · 100 MPH · STRENGTHENED FROM CAT 1 · NO LANDFALL
major_events.impact: Hurricane Marie strengthened to Category 2 with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph as of September 4, up from the Category 1 (80 mph) designation in September 3 reporting. The storm continues tracking west-northwestward off the Mexican coast. No landfall is forecast. With Hurricane Karina forecast to become post-tropical by Monday, Marie represents the remaining Eastern Pacific system alongside Lowell. The Super El Niño sea surface temperature anomalies sustaining the eastern Pacific warm pool continue to support above-normal tropical cyclone activity.

major_events.name: Hurricane Karina (Eastern Pacific) — Forecast Post-Tropical by Monday; No Hawaii Threat; Dissipating
major_events.status: WEAKENING · FORECAST POST-TROPICAL BY MONDAY · NO HAWAII THREAT · DISSIPATING
major_events.impact: Hurricane Karina continues weakening in hostile conditions — drier air intrusion, lower sea surface temperatures, and increasing vertical wind shear — as forecast. NHC expects Karina to become post-tropical by Monday before dissipating entirely. No threat to Hawaii. The dual-major-hurricane convergence scenario for Hawaii that was elevated on September 2–3 has been eliminated; Lowell's track alone now represents the Hawaiian Islands threat.

major_events.name: Europe Wildfire and Drought Emergency — ONGOING: 647,375 ha Burned; Very Extreme Fire Danger Through September 9; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed
major_events.status: ONGOING · 647,375 HA · VERY EXTREME FIRE DANGER THROUGH SEPT 9 · RHINE LOWEST SINCE 1880
major_events.impact: JRC EFFIS reports EU-wide burnt area at 647,375 hectares with no significant new boundary change reported for September 5. Very extreme fire danger continues through September 9 across Iberia, France, the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. The atmospheric blocking pattern has strengthened rather than broken. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues to curtail output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances.

major_events.name: Pakistan Monsoon Flooding — ONGOING: 299+ Dead; Heavy Rains Hit Islamabad / Rawalpindi September 1 (197 mm); NDMA Forecasts 2–3 More September Pulse Events
major_events.status: ONGOING · 299+ DEAD · ISLAMABAD/RAWALPINDI SEPT 1 FLOODING · PEAK MONSOON · 2–3 MORE SPELLS
major_events.impact: Pakistan's cumulative monsoon season death toll stands at 299 (including 140 children) per the most recent NDMA reporting. On September 1, torrential rains beginning at 3:20 a.m. inundated Islamabad and Rawalpindi: Shamsabad recorded 197 mm in roughly 5 hours — the heaviest downpour in three years — while the Nullah Lai river approached dangerous flood levels. Both cities closed all schools and sought Army assistance. NDMA continues to forecast 2–3 additional monsoon pulse events during September — the season's climatological peak — with this year's rainfall running 50–60% heavier than the comparable period last year.

major_events.name: BC Bald Range Wildfire — HELD: ~25,163 Hectares; Phased Re-Entry Assessment; 379 Firefighters Active
major_events.impact: BC Wildfire Service's HELD classification for the Bald Range wildfire near Summerland is maintained with no material change from September 4. The fire has burned approximately 25,163 hectares. 379 wildland firefighters, 7 helicopters, and 43 pieces of heavy equipment remain assigned. Evacuation orders and alerts remain active for portions of Summerland (population 12,000) and Peachland. A phased re-entry assessment continues for lower-risk zones. Cooler weather and rainfall since August 28 continue to aid suppression.

weather.overview_html: The pivotal shift on September 5 is Hurricane Lowell’s re-intensification to Category 5 (160 mph) — only the 8th such storm in the central Pacific on record and the first since Walaka in 2018 — prompting Hawaii Governor Josh Green to declare a statewide emergency, with CPHC warning that hurricane watches for Kauai County could be required as soon as Saturday and the center forecast to approach the western Hawaiian Islands late Monday. In South Asia, the Nepal–Tibet GLOF death toll has risen to at least 1,318 (1,287 in Nepal, 31 in Tibet) with 5,614+ still missing. Malaysia escalated sharply: King Sultan Ibrahim declared a formal emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak, after the Air Pollutant Index peaked at 521 — the highest emergency-threshold breach of the 2026 haze season, with 647 schools closing and a cloud-seeding operation launched. Meanwhile, Hurricane Marie has strengthened from Category 1 to Category 2 (100 mph) in the Eastern Pacific.

items.headline: Hurricane Lowell Re-Intensifies to Category 5 (160 mph); Hawaii Statewide Emergency Declared; CPHC: Kauai County Watches Expected Saturday; Sharp North Turn Sunday; Kauai Late Monday; Only 8th Central-Pacific Cat 5 on Record
items.summary: Hurricane Lowell re-intensified to Category 5 with maximum sustained winds near 160 mph as of the September 4 5 p.m. CPHC advisory, recovering from the Category 4 (140 mph) intensity reported earlier on September 4. Lowell is only the eighth Category 5 hurricane in the central Pacific basin on record, and the first since Hurricane Walaka in 2018. It completed rapid intensification from a 70-mph tropical storm to a 160-mph Category 5 in just over 30 hours — one of the fastest intensifications ever recorded in the central Pacific. Governor Josh Green signed a statewide emergency proclamation covering all of Hawaii on September 4, allowing pre-positioning of state and county resources. CPHC forecasters warned that hurricane watches could be required for portions of Kauai County on Saturday — the first formal warning-class action since Lowell's formation. The storm is forecast to drift westward through Saturday before a sharp turn to the north on Sunday under a weakening mid-level ridge, bringing it to near-major hurricane strength in the vicinity of the western Hawaiian Islands late Monday and Monday night. Heavy rainfall from outer bands is expected to bring 3 to 6 inches to Kauai and the Big Island, with localized totals exceeding 10 inches and the potential for flash flooding and mudslides in areas of steep terrain.

items.source: Wikipedia / Al Jazeera / PBS NewsHour / NBC News
items.headline: Nepal–Tibet GLOF: STATUS CHANGE — 1,287+ Confirmed Dead in Nepal + 31 in Tibet; 5,083+ Missing Nepal + 531 Tibet; Flood Debris Reaches India 240 km Away; One of Deadliest GLOFs on Record
items.summary: Updated September 5 figures confirm at least 1,287 people dead in Nepal and 31 in Tibet, with 5,083 missing in Nepal and 531 missing in Tibet — a combined minimum toll of at least 1,318 dead and 5,614 missing, substantially higher than the 1,100 dead and 4,500 missing counts from September 4. Flood debris has now been recovered 240 km downstream of the event origin inside India. Chinese authorities maintain their warning that surrounding glaciers 'may still collapse, posing significant potential risks.' An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. The disaster originated from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung at approximately 5,200 metres elevation, generating a seismic signal of magnitude Ms 5.2 detected globally. The event represents one of the deadliest glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) on instrumental record globally, amplified by the accelerating instability of Himalayan glaciers under Super El Niño baseline ocean and atmospheric warming.

items.headline: Malaysia Declares Emergency in Serian Division, Sarawak — Air Pollutant Index Peaked at 521; 647 Schools to Close Monday; Cloud-Seeding Launched; Singapore 3rd Worst Air Quality Globally; Indonesia 717 Hot Spots

King Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration; Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's office announced 647 schools will close from Monday until at least the end of next week. Malaysia launched a three-day cloud-seeding operation to attempt precipitation. Serian remained at hazardous-level API readings (376) as of September 5 morning. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry satellite data shows 717 fire hot spots nationally since August 1 and 103 active in the past 24 hours. Singapore recorded the third-worst air quality globally on September 4 by IQAir. Indonesia's El Niño-driven dry season is expected to maintain elevated fire risk through early October across Kalimantan, which is the primary fire-source province for the regional haze.

items.headline: Hurricane Marie Strengthens to Category 2 (100 mph); Upgraded From Category 1 (80 mph); No Landfall Forecast; Super El Niño SSTs Supporting Eastern Pacific Activity
items.summary: Hurricane Marie strengthened to Category 2 status with maximum sustained winds near 100 mph and a minimum central pressure of 972 mb as of September 4 advisories, up from Category 1 at 80 mph. Located near 19.9°N, 117.1°W and moving west-northwestward. No landfall is forecast. With Hurricane Karina forecast to become post-tropical by Monday, Marie and Lowell represent the two remaining active Pacific systems. The above-normal sea surface temperatures sustained by Super El Niño thermodynamics across the eastern and central Pacific continue to support above-normal tropical cyclone development during the peak of the hurricane season.

renewables.overview_html: No major new project or deal announcements emerged on September 5 in the renewables sector. The week’s leading milestone remains the September 1 installation of the first of 53 monopiles at OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII), RWE and TotalEnergies’ 795 MW North Sea project using Vestas V236-15 MW turbines, scheduled to supply ~1 million Dutch households by early 2028. In the US structural story, EIA data confirm solar, wind and storage added 44,889 MW in the year to June 2026 versus only 7,530 MW for natural gas, with combined renewable installed capacity on pace to surpass the entire gas fleet within approximately 12 months, reinforced by the IEA’s Electricity Mid-Year Update 2026 finding that global renewable generation is set to overtake coal-fired output in 2026 for the first time. The federal–state collision continues: California’s lawsuit over the Trump administration’s $120 million buyout of the 2 GW Golden State Wind lease proceeds. UK plug-in solar remains a live consumer market after SI 2026/848 legalised 800 W residential socket systems from August 27, now available at 800+ Argos stores.

items.headline: OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) First Monopile Installed — 795 MW RWE/TotalEnergies JV; 53 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbines; 53 km Off Dutch Coast; 1 Million Dutch Households by 2028; Transition-Piece-Less Design
items.summary: The offshore installation vessel Les Alizés successfully installed the first of 53 monopiles for OranjeWind (Hollandse Kust West VII) on September 1, 53 km west of IJmuiden in the Dutch North Sea. The 795 MW project is a joint venture between RWE and TotalEnergies, using 53 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines — among the largest offshore turbines commercially deployed. The project uses innovative transition-piece-less monopiles, where turbine towers bolt directly to the monopile without a transition piece, reducing steel per foundation. Installation of all 53 monopiles is expected to complete by early 2027; turbine installation in 2027; fully operational by early 2028, supplying approximately 1 million Dutch households.

items.headline: EIA Data: US Renewables Installed Capacity to Surpass Natural Gas Within 12 Months — Solar+Wind Added 44,889 MW vs. Gas’s 7,530 MW in Year to June 2026; Battery Storage Up 17,859 MW
items.summary: New EIA capacity data show US renewable energy installed capacity is on pace to surpass natural gas within approximately 12 months — most likely by summer 2027. In the year through June 30, 2026: utility-scale solar added 28,077 MW; small-scale solar 6,492 MW; wind 10,553 MW; combined renewables 44,889 MW. Natural gas capacity grew only 7,530 MW in the same period. Battery storage added 17,859 MW. When combined renewables capacity eventually exceeds natural gas's installed base, it will mark a structural inflection in the US power system.

items.headline: California Sues Trump Administration Over $120 Million Deal to Cancel 2 GW Golden State Wind Offshore Lease; Alleges Violations of Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act; $100M in Port/Transmission Prep Already Spent
items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the California Energy Commission filed suit August 28 challenging the Interior Department's agreement to pay $120 million to abandon the 2 GW Golden State Wind offshore lease and invest instead in fossil fuel projects. The complaint alleges violations of the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, the Judgment Fund Act, and other federal statutes. The 2 GW project would have supplied clean electricity to more than 1 million California homes. California notes it has already spent more than $100 million on port upgrades, transmission improvements, and other infrastructure in preparation for the project.

items.headline: UK Plug-In Solar Panels Legal Across Great Britain From August 27 — SI 2026/848 Enables 800 W Residential Systems Via Standard Sockets; Available at 800+ Argos Stores; Saves Up to £110/Year
items.summary: Plug-in solar panels became legal for residential use across England, Wales, and Scotland from August 27, 2026, under Plug-In Solar Amendment SI 2026/848. The regulation allows compliant systems with a maximum rated AC output of 800 W to connect via a standard plug without planning permission or a certified electrician — creating a legal pathway similar to Germany, France, and the Netherlands. Systems are immediately available at over 800 Argos stores and are estimated to save households up to £110 per year.

science.overview_html: The standout new paper on September 5 is arXiv:2609.03210 (Schmitt et al., September 2, 2026), which fine-tunes a graph-transformer AI weather architecture with IMERG precipitation observational data at 0.25° resolution, achieving up to 19% improvement in medium-range continuous ranked probability scores and a 57% Brier skill score improvement on extreme rainfall over state-of-the-art operational models — directly relevant as Hurricane Lowell threatens Hawaii and Pakistan and Nepal face active extreme precipitation events. The dominant story from September 3 carries forward: Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 3 (arXiv:2609.03582) — the first global AI weather model to train on raw observations and ingest live geostationary satellite data, achieving hourly 5-km surface resolution, 60% better precipitation vs. WeatherNext 2, and topping Brightband’s WeatherBench benchmark, now live in Google Search, Gemini and Maps. Also in the rolling window: arXiv:2608.30795’s probabilistic Aardvark Weather, demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition improves mean forecast skill by 4.2%; and the GRL study detecting 245 glacial earthquakes at Thwaites 2010–2023, with the 2018–2020 cluster coinciding with episodic glacier acceleration — directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster evolves.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03210: Fine-Tuning AI Weather Model With IMERG Precipitation Observations Improves Medium-Range CRPS by Up to 19% and Extreme Rainfall Brier Skill by 57%; Tropical Storms and Drizzle Also Improved
items.meta: Schmitt, Delorme, King, Patodia, Schneider, Sheshadri, Jain · arXiv:2609.03210 · September 2, 2026
items.summary: Artificial intelligence weather prediction (AIWP) systems now surpass state-of-the-art physical models for medium-range forecasting, but current global AIWP models are trained almost exclusively on the ERA5 reanalysis, which has known biases particularly for precipitation. This paper fine-tunes a graph-transformer AIWP architecture directly with IMERG precipitation observational data at 0.25° resolution. Results: medium-range continuous ranked probability scores (CRPS) improve by up to 19%; Brier skill score for extreme rainfall prediction improves by 57% globally over state-of-the-art operational NWP models. The fine-tuned model also demonstrates superior skill for tropical storm precipitation and drizzle events. The approach is directly relevant to today's acute precipitation hazards: Hurricane Lowell threatening Hawaii, Pakistan's monsoon, and Nepal's ongoing flood disaster. The work reinforces a broader finding that closing the gap between AI model training and real observational data improves both average and tail-risk forecast performance.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 5-km Global AI Weather Model Trains on Raw Observations; 60% Better Precipitation vs. WN2; 100-m Wind-Height Forecasts for Turbines; Tops Brightband WeatherBench; Live in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based AI models and shrinking it to 3–4 hours with hourly forecast cycles. Resolution: 5 km for key surface variables, 10 km for other surface variables, 25 km for atmospheric variables, and explicit 100-meter hub-height wind forecasts for wind turbine applications alongside cloud cover and solar radiation for grid operators. WeatherNext 3 has 2.4x more parameters than WeatherNext 2. Precipitation evaluation shows CRPS improvements of up to 60% against IMERG and 50% Brier score reduction versus NWP baselines at early lead times. On Brightband's Operational WeatherBench, WeatherNext 3 ranks first across temperature, wind speed, and humidity. Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Google Earth Engine.

items.source: arXiv / Barcelona Supercomputing Center / ECML PKDD 2026
items.headline: arXiv 2609.00847: First Comprehensive Checklist for Energy and Carbon Footprints of ML/AI in Earth System Modeling; Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Presented at GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026 Naples
items.meta: Dainelli, Mozaffari, Castaño et al. (BSC Earth Dept.) · arXiv:2609.00847 · September 1, 2026 · GREEN-AI Workshop, ECML PKDD 2026, Naples
items.summary: As machine learning finds its way into nearly every aspect of Earth system modeling, this Barcelona Supercomputing Center paper provides the first comprehensive checklist for ML/AI practitioners to assess and reduce the environmental footprint of their applications. The checklist is organized around successive pipeline stages — data curation, model architecture, training regime, inference, and deployment — with curated metrics for estimating energy consumption and carbon footprint at each stage. The work is timely given the explosive growth of compute-intensive neural weather models and raises the question of whether the carbon cost of training and running these models is systematically accounted for. Presented at the GREEN-AI workshop of ECML PKDD 2026 in Naples.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.30795: Uncertainty-Aware End-to-End AI Weather Forecasting — Aardvark Weather Made Probabilistic; Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty Decomposed; Probabilistic Fine-Tuning Improves Mean Forecast 4.2%
items.meta: Almeida, Otero, Arndt, Baur, Samek, Ma · arXiv:2608.30795 · Submitted 31 Aug 2026
items.summary: This paper renders the Aardvark Weather end-to-end AI weather system probabilistic by attaching two stochastic mechanisms: (1) learned, input-dependent noise at the observation encoder capturing aleatoric uncertainty; (2) Monte Carlo dropout in the processor capturing epistemic uncertainty. A law-of-total-variance decomposition attributes forecast spread to each source. Key result: probabilistic fine-tuning improves the mean forecast by 4.2% on average across variables and lead times — demonstrating that uncertainty decomposition and mean-forecast skill are mutually reinforcing rather than in tension.

items.headline: GRL: 245 Glacial Earthquakes Detected at Thwaites “Doomsday Glacier” Marine Edge 2010–2023 — Busiest Cluster 2018–2020 Coincided With Episodic Glacier Acceleration
items.meta: Pham et al. (Australian National University) · Geophysical Research Letters · Published 29 Aug 2026
items.summary: A study in Geophysical Research Letters presents the first systematic detection of 245 previously uncatalogued seismic events near Thwaites Glacier's marine edge, catalogued over 2010–2023. Most are likely glacial earthquakes caused by capsizing, calving icebergs colliding with the parent glacier. The 2018–2020 cluster was the busiest, coinciding with episodic acceleration of Thwaites' floating ice tongue toward the sea. The findings add seismic evidence to the broad body of research showing Thwaites' marine-based instability is accelerating — directly relevant as the Nepal–Tibet GLOF disaster underscores the expanding global glacial hazard under anthropogenic warming.

items.headline: arXiv 2608.26822 (Nested-EAGLE): Single ML System Bridges 0.25° Global and 6-km Regional Forecasting Over CONUS; Lower MSE Than Both GFS and HRRR for Near-Surface Fields
items.summary: A NOAA team introduces Nested-EAGLE, an ML weather prediction system that unifies short-range and medium-range forecasting in a single architecture — combining a 0.25° global model with a 6 km refinement over CONUS. Nested-EAGLE achieves significantly lower mean-squared error in near-surface and low-level quantities over CONUS compared to both GFS and HRRR, while remaining competitive globally. The unified short-and-medium-range system provides an improved distillation of global weather to local impacts from a single model.

items.headline: ECMWF Operationally Deploys AIFL: LSTM Global Streamflow Model Trained on 18,588 Basins; Detects 20-Year Flood Signal 6 Days in Advance; Enters Copernicus EMS Flood Service
items.summary: ECMWF's operationally deployed AIFL (AI for Floods) LSTM, trained on 18,588 river basins from the CARAVAN dataset, detects a 20-year return-level flood signal six days in advance — demonstrated during Storm Henk (Belgium, January 2024). The deployment within Copernicus Emergency Management Service provides global flood early warning directly relevant to the current extreme precipitation events in Pakistan, Nepal, and Southeast Asia.

items.title: Cyclic Materials Closes $75 Million Series C Led by T. Rowe Price to Scale US Rare Earth Recycling — Total Equity Now $237 Million; Arizona Facility Operational Q3 2026; South Carolina Campus Breaking Ground Q4; Critical Supply for Wind Turbines and EV Magnets
items.body_html: Cyclic Materials, a Canadian rare earth recycling company, closed a $75 million Series C financing round announced September 2, 2026, led by accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates, bringing total equity funding to $237 million. Strategic investor ERI joined the round alongside existing backers Microsoft, Amazon, and others. Cyclic’s Hub-and-Spoke system recovers rare earth materials from permanent magnets in end-of-life wind turbines, EV motors, and manufacturing scrap, converting them into high-purity rare earth oxides — directly reducing Western dependence on Chinese primary rare earth supply. An Arizona magnet separation and critical mineral recycling plant is expected to begin operations during Q3 2026, with a South Carolina integrated rare earth recycling campus breaking ground in Q4 2026.
items.source_html: Cyclic Materials / Metal Tech News

items.title: Artemis London 2026: Cat Bond and ILS Market Well-Positioned for Disciplined Growth; AFME Calls for ILS to Back Climate Policies; 220 Attendees, 120+ Organizations; London Bridge Cat Bonds and LoC Capital Stacks Discussed
items.body_html: The Artemis London 2026 conference on September 1 convened approximately 220 attendees from more than 120 organizations across the ILS ecosystem, including specialists, (re)insurance buyers, investors, fund managers, and service providers. Speakers highlighted discipline in the catastrophe bond market and expected continued growth. The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME) called for ILS and catastrophe bonds as effective mechanisms for insurers to access new capital to back climate-related policies — directly relevant as the Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report, released the same day, put average annual insured losses at a record $171 billion. The convergence of ILS market growth, the Verisk benchmark revision, Hurricane Lowell’s Hawaii threat, and the Nepal–Tibet disaster illustrates the direct line from extreme weather under Super El Niño to capital markets.

items.title: Verisk 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report: Industry Should Prepare for $171 Billion Average Annual Insured Losses — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; US Accounts for $117B (68%); 100-Year Loss at $477B; Highest Estimate Verisk Has Ever Reported
items.body_html: Verisk released its 2026 Global Modeled Catastrophe Losses Report on September 1, calculating that the insurance industry should be prepared to absorb $171 billion in insured catastrophe losses on an average annual basis — up $19 billion from the prior-year estimate and the highest average annual loss figure Verisk has ever published. Of the $171 billion global insured AAL, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States; the 100-year return-period scenario yields $477 billion in aggregate insured losses, and the 250-year scenario reaches $606 billion. A companion release covers Europe: Europe carries $110 billion in expected annual economic catastrophe losses, of which only about $24 billion is currently insured — a protection gap of roughly 78%. Severe thunderstorm accounts for 40% of modelled risk, followed by tropical cyclone (27%), earthquake (10%), winter storm (9%), flood (7%), and wildfire (6%).
items.source_html: GlobeNewswire / Verisk / Insurance Journal

items.title: Redstone Closes €25 Million First Tranche of Blue Economy Decarbonization Fund — Targeting Maritime Carbon Reduction, Ocean Asset Security, and Coastal Infrastructure Resilience
items.body_html: Berlin- and Helsinki-based fund manager Redstone closed the first tranche of its blue economy decarbonization fund at €25 million during the week of August 28, targeting investments in technologies to decarbonize maritime sectors, secure ocean-based assets, and build resilient coastal infrastructure. The fund addresses a sector responsible for approximately 2.5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Alternative fuels (ammonia, methanol, green hydrogen), hull efficiency technologies, and port electrification represent core investment themes. The first close reflects growing investor interest in maritime decarbonization as the IMO’s strengthened 2050 net-zero shipping target creates regulatory pull.

items.title: BlocPower Shuts Down and Liquidates — Community Clean Energy Electrification Platform Winds Down After 14 Years; Returns Capital to Investors
items.body_html: BlocPower, the community-focused clean energy company that electrified buildings in low-income urban neighborhoods by replacing gas heating with heat pumps and solar, is shutting down and liquidating its assets, returning remaining capital to investors. BlocPower had operated since 2012, achieving significant attention for decarbonizing community buildings in underserved neighborhoods across New York City and other markets. The closure is a notable setback for impact-oriented community climate tech and underscores the structural challenges facing mission-driven platforms trying to deploy clean energy in underserved markets at scale.
